dismissed.reason: Guarded: Stars returns early when rating === null (Stars.tsx:2).
public/index.html always contains <div id="root">, so getElementById('root') cannot be null.
parts[i] is always defined: the loop skips patterns whose length differs from parts (routes.ts:23).

crashes.title: Theme saved by version 0.2.0 crashes the app on every launch

locations.role: same unguarded read; also throws SecurityError where the browser blocks storage
called during render, outside any boundary

trigger.description: localStorage 'pantry.prefs' holds the plain string 'dark' (or 'light'), as written by 0.2.0; JSON.parse throws SyntaxError while Header renders.
trigger.basis: CHANGELOG.md:9: 0.2.0 saved the theme name in pantry.prefs; 0.3.0 reads the same key as JSON with no migration. Every user who chose a theme in 0.2.0 has this value.

boundary.note: Header renders outside RouteBoundary and there is no root boundary, so React unmounts the whole tree; the stored value survives reloads.

trace.note: 0.2.0 stored the theme name, not JSON, under pantry.prefs
<Header /> sits outside <RouteBoundary>; main.tsx has no root boundary

ranking.likelihood_basis: Real stored data for every upgraded user who picked a theme in 0.2.0

preconditions: A browser profile that used Pantry 0.2.0 and chose the dark theme (or seed the value below)
steps: Set localStorage 'pantry.prefs' to 'dark' for the app's origin
repro.expected: The app loads with the dark theme, or falls back to defaults
repro.actual: Blank page on first load and after every reload; SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'd', "dark" is not valid JSON
repro.stack_trace:
SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'd', "dark" is not valid JSON
    at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
    at loadPrefs (http://localhost:4173/app.js:23844:41)
    at Header (http://localhost:4173/app.js:23853:19)
    at Object.react_stack_bottom_frame (http://localhost:4173/app.js:21553:22)
    at renderWithHooks (http://localhost:4173/app.js:7212:26)
    at updateFunctionComponent (http://localhost:4173/app.js:9057:24)

crashes.remediation: Read preferences through a safe loader: wrap storage access and JSON.parse in try/catch, migrate a bare theme name to {theme}, and fall back to defaults. Add a root error boundary so a shell error cannot blank the whole app.
crashes.verification_step: python repro/repro_C-1.py exits 0 (no uncaught error, app renders) with pantry.prefs = 'dark', 'light' and '{'

crashes.title: An imported recipe (no author) breaks the recipe list

trigger.description: GET /api/recipes returns any item with "author": null; r.author.displayName throws TypeError during render.
trigger.basis: openapi.json:46 marks RecipeSummary.author nullable ("null for recipes imported from a URL"); src/types.ts:13 says the same, but tsconfig has strict off so the compiler never flags it.

boundary.note: RouteBoundary shows "Something went wrong"; the header still works.

trace.note: listRecipes() passes the response through unvalidated

ranking.likelihood_basis: Contract-valid; happens as soon as one imported recipe is in the list

preconditions: At least one recipe imported from a URL
steps: Mock GET /api/recipes to include an item with "author": null
repro.expected: The list shows the imported recipe (e.g. "Imported recipe" instead of an author)
repro.actual: The whole list is replaced by "Something went wrong"
repro.stack_trace:
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'displayName')
    at http://localhost:4173/app.js:23922:18
    at Array.map (<anonymous>)
    at RecipeList (http://localhost:4173/app.js:23917:105)
    at Object.react_stack_bottom_frame (http://localhost:4173/app.js:21553:22)
    at renderWithHooks (http://localhost:4173/app.js:7212:26)
    at updateFunctionComponent (http://localhost:4173/app.js:9057:24)

crashes.remediation: Render r.author?.displayName ?? 'Imported recipe' (as RecipeDetail already does), and turn on strictNullChecks so the compiler catches the rest.
crashes.verification_step: python repro/repro_C-2.py exits 0; the list renders the imported recipe

crashes.title: A recipe with no ratings yet cannot be opened

trigger.description: GET /api/recipes/{id} returns "rating": null (ratingCount 0); recipe.rating.toFixed(1) throws TypeError during render.
trigger.basis: openapi.json:49: rating is "null until the recipe has at least one rating", so every newly published recipe has it. The list guards it (Stars.tsx:2); the detail page does not.

preconditions: A published recipe with no ratings
repro.actual: The recipe page is replaced by "Something went wrong"
repro.stack_trace:
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'toFixed')
    at RecipeDetail (http://localhost:4173/app.js:23974:23)
    at Object.react_stack_bottom_frame (http://localhost:4173/app.js:21553:22)
    at renderWithHooks (http://localhost:4173/app.js:7212:26)
    at updateFunctionComponent (http://localhost:4173/app.js:9057:24)
    at beginWork (http://localhost:4173/app.js:10137:22)
    at runWithFiberInDEV (http://localhost:4173/app.js:2427:74)

crashes.remediation: Reuse <Stars rating={recipe.rating} count={recipe.ratingCount} />, which already handles null.
crashes.verification_step: python repro/repro_C-3.py exits 0; the page shows "No ratings yet"

crashes.title: Recipe page crashes on iOS 16 and Safari before 17.4 (Object.groupBy missing)

trigger.description: Open any recipe in Safari on iOS 16 to 17.3 or macOS Safari before 17.4: Object.groupBy is undefined, so the call throws TypeError during render.
trigger.basis: package.json:23 declares "iOS >= 16" as a supported target; Object.groupBy shipped in Safari 17.4 (and Chrome 117, Firefox 119). esbuild does not polyfill it.

trace.note: Object.groupBy called on every recipe render

ranking.likelihood_basis: Only browsers within the declared targets that predate Safari 17.4

environment.browser: Safari 17.3 or earlier (iOS 16 device or simulator)

steps: On an iOS 16 device, open the app
repro.actual: Not observed. By the trace, the page is replaced by "Something went wrong" (TypeError: Object.groupBy is not a function)
repro.not_reproduced_reason: Playwright WebKit ships a current Safari engine that has Object.groupBy; no iOS 16 device was available.

crashes.remediation: Group with a small reduce() helper (or add a core-js polyfill), or deliberately raise the declared iOS target to 17.4.
crashes.verification_step: Open a recipe in Safari 17.3 (or with Object.groupBy deleted in an init script) and confirm it renders

crashes.title: A malformed recipe link blanks the whole app

locations.role: called during App render, outside any boundary

trigger.description: Open a recipe link whose id has a broken percent-escape, e.g. /#/recipes/%E0%A4%A (a truncated link pasted from a chat app); decodeURIComponent throws URIError.
trigger.basis: Recipe links are shared (RT-2), and truncated or hand-edited links are common; the hash is decoded in App render before any boundary.

boundary.note: match() runs in App itself, so nothing can catch it; the hashchange listener is gone after the unmount, so Back does not recover.

trace.note: no root boundary; React unmounts the app

ranking.likelihood_basis: Needs a malformed link; happens by accident but rarely

repro.stack_trace:
URIError: URI malformed
    at decodeURIComponent (<anonymous>)
    at http://localhost:4173/app.js:24038:32
    at Array.every (<anonymous>)
    at match (http://localhost:4173/app.js:24036:26)
    at App (http://localhost:4173/app.js:24057:31)
    at Object.react_stack_bottom_frame (http://localhost:4173/app.js:21553:22)

crashes.remediation: Decode inside try/catch and treat a malformed segment as no match; add a root error boundary.

trigger.description: GET /api/recipes/{id} without a "nutrition" key; nutrition.calories throws TypeError.
trigger.basis: openapi.json:83: nutrition is optional, "only present once the nutrition job has run".

boundary.note: PanelBoundary shows "Not available right now."; the rest of the recipe works.

repro.actual: Panel shows "Not available right now." for a recipe that simply has no data yet

degradations.title: Recipe page stays on "Loading…" forever when the request fails

trigger.description: GET /api/recipes/{id} returns 404 or 500 (deleted recipe, server error) or the device is offline.
trigger.basis: openapi.json declares a 404 response; api.ts:5 throws on any non-2xx.

boundary.note: Unhandled promise rejection; the article area never leaves the loading state.

trace.note: no rejection handler; recipe stays null

degradations.remediation: Handle the rejection like RecipeList does: show "Recipe not found" or "Couldn't load recipe" with a retry.
degradations.verification_step: Mock a 404 for the recipe: an error message appears instead of an endless "Loading…"

degradations.title: Changing a setting throws when storage is full or blocked

trigger.description: localStorage.setItem throws QuotaExceededError (storage full) or SecurityError (storage blocked) when the user changes theme or units.
trigger.basis: Called from the select onChange handler (Settings.tsx:8); not traced further.

boundary.note: Thrown in an event handler, which error boundaries do not catch; React keeps the screen, the setting is not saved.

degradations.remediation: Save through the same safe storage wrapper as the C-1 fix, and tell the user if the setting could not be saved.
degradations.verification_step: Stub setItem to throw: the select still changes and a message explains the setting was not saved

limitations: Probes ran in one browser engine (Chromium 156) with mocked API responses; no real backend, device or older Safari was used.
ESLint and Semgrep did not run (not configured / not installed), so hook-dependency loops and floating promises were only checked by pattern.
Field-name matching in the contract diff can miss accesses after destructuring; the strict tsc overlay covered those here.
No production telemetry was provided, so likelihoods come from the contract, the changelog and the declared targets.
next_steps: Fix C-1 first: it blanks the app for every upgraded user who chose a theme, on every launch.
Add a root error boundary in main.tsx; C-1 and C-4 would then become screen-level instead of white screens.
Turn on strictNullChecks: the strict overlay found the C-2, C-3 and D-1 accesses mechanically.
Keep the repro specs as regression checks once the fixes land (each exits 0 when fixed).

summary.headline: 5 likely crashes, 4 of them reproduced: a P0 crash loop for users upgrading from 0.2.0, and two contract-valid responses that break the recipe list and recipe page.
